'''Gordon John Van Wylen''' (February 6, 1920 – November 5, 2020)<ref>{{Cite web |title=76409466 |url=https://viaf.org/viaf/76409466/ |website=viaf.org}}</ref> was an American engineer and educator, known for his textbooks on [[thermodynamics]]. He served as the 9th president of [[Hope College]] from 1972 to 1987 and as the 8th dean of the [[University of Michigan College of Engineering]] from 1965 to 1972.

==Biography==
Van Wylen was born in [[Grant, Michigan]]. He served in the [[United States Navy]] during [[World War II]]. 

He received a bachelor's degree from [[Calvin University|Calvin College]], a master's degree from [[University of Michigan]], and a doctorate degree from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=#GivingTuesday |url=https://dayofgiving.hope.edu/ |access-date=2020-11-26 |website=dayofgiving.hope.edu |language=en}}</ref>{{When|date=July 2021}} 

In 1959, he published a textbook ''Thermodynamics'', in which he stated a belief in "a Creator" in his summation of the [[second law of thermodynamics]]. “A final point to be made is that the second law of thermodynamics and the principle of increase in [[entropy]] have great philosophical implications. The question that arises is how did the universe get into the state of reduced entropy in the first place, since all natural processes known to us tend to increase entropy? ... The author has found that the second law tends to increase his conviction that there is a Creator who has the answer for the future destiny of man and the universe.”{{sfn|Van Wylen|1959|p=169}}

He was chair of the Engineering Department at the [[University of Michigan]] from 1969 to 1972. He was appointed president of Hope College in [[Holland, Michigan]], in 1972, serving until his retirement in 1987. He died of complications from [[COVID-19]] in Holland, on November 5, 2020, at the age of 100, during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Olgers |first=Greg |date=2020-11-05 |title=Former Hope College President Gordon Van Wylen Dies |url=https://hope.edu/news/2020/campus-life/former-hope-college-president-gordon-van-wylen-dies.html |access-date=2020-11-05 |website=Hope College |language=en}}</ref>
